title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 226 (Enforcement and consequences of agent’s contracts)

content.overview: Section 226 provides that contracts entered into through an agent, and obligations arising from acts done by an agent, may be enforced in the same manner, and will have the same legal consequences, as if the contracts had been entered into and the acts done by the principal in person.
content.glance: Agent’s authorised contracts and acts → same enforcement and consequences as if done by the principal in person.
content.study: Contracts entered into through an agent, and obligations arising from acts done by an agent, may be enforced in the same manner, and will have the same legal consequences, as if the contracts had been entered into and the acts done by the principal in person. This is the core attribution rule of agency: within authority, the agent’s contracting and acting bind and benefit the principal as the principal’s own. Current-law framing: identify the contract or act; test agency and authority; apply same-manner / same-consequences enforcement.

sections.heading: Contracts through an agent
sections.body: Contracts entered into through an agent may be enforced as if entered into by the principal in person.

sections.heading: Obligations from agent’s acts
sections.body: Obligations arising from acts done by an agent have the same legal consequences as if done by the principal in person.

provisions.title: Enforcement and consequences of agent’s contracts

examples.title: Sale by authorised agent
examples.body: An authorised agent sells goods for the principal. The buyer may enforce the sale against the principal as if the principal had sold in person.

hypotheticals.question: Does section 226 apply to unauthorised acts?
hypotheticals.analysis: Section 226 assumes the agent’s contracts and acts are within the agency framework. Excess of authority is governed by ss. 227–228; ostensible authority and related rules appear elsewhere in Chapter X.

distinctions.title: Attribution of authorised acts (s. 226) vs excess of authority (s. 227)
distinctions.left: Same enforcement as principal in person

misconceptions.trap: Only the agent can be sued on a contract made through the agent.
misconceptions.correction: Section 226 attributes enforcement and consequences to the principal as if the principal had contracted in person.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 226 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify the contract or act. II. Confirm agency and authority. III. Apply same-manner / same-consequences rule. IV. Address excess under ss. 227–228 if raised. V. Conclude.

examTips: Link to excess rules in ss. 227–228.
